title: Function Contracts and Testing
learningObjectives: Identify the function's role, inputs and control flow.
Trace calls, local state and returned results.
Recognize common design or safety mistakes.
Write and test a reusable function for a practical task.

understand.concept: A function contract describes expected inputs, outputs, preconditions, postconditions and constraints. Testing checks whether actual behavior matches that contract.
understand.whyItMatters: Explicit contracts make functions easier to use safely and easier to test independently.
understand.explain: Test typical inputs, boundary values and invalid inputs. Avoid undefined behavior. Prefer deterministic functions with limited side effects. Use assertions or explicit failure results where appropriate, and never rely only on a successful compile.

examples.title: Checked division
examples.code: bool divide(double a,double b,double& result){if(b==0.0)return false;result=a/b;return true;}
examples.explanation: The function checks a precondition and reports success or failure; output is set only on success.

examples.title: Boundary tests
examples.explanation: Values adjacent to limits verify boundary behavior.

examples.title: Threshold test
examples.code: bool isAdult(int age){return age>=18;}\n// Check 17, 18 and 19
examples.explanation: Adjacent values help expose off-by-one errors.

examples.title: Pure calculation
examples.code: int triple(int x){return 3*x;}\n// Caller can compare or print the returned result
examples.explanation: A simple input-output function is easy to test.

examples.title: Reject empty collection
examples.code: int first(const std::vector<int>& v){if(v.empty())throw std::invalid_argument(\"empty\");return v.front();}
examples.explanation: The function checks emptiness before accessing the first element.

practise.guidedTask: Walk through all five Function Contracts and Testing examples. Annotate the signature, call arguments, local state, control flow, return behavior and side effects.
practise.independentTask: Document a precondition and postcondition for three functions. Build a test table containing typical, boundary and invalid inputs. Explain what happens when a precondition is violated.
hints: Start with the function signature and intended contract.
Trace each call with a small input.
Separate calculation from output when appropriate.
Test normal, boundary and invalid cases.
Check lifetimes, side effects and termination.

questions.explanation: Adjacent values cover the threshold edge.
